question: A Scottish statin trial cut five-year heart attacks from 7.9% to 5.5%. Men treated per attack prevented, to the nearest whole number?
answer: About 42 men treated for five years per heart attack prevented
move: Turn every risk cut into people treated for one person helped.
ask: When a pill or plan promises to cut a risk, do I know how many people take it for one to benefit?
trap: Reading the 31% relative cut as 31 men helped in every 100.
hint: Subtract the two percentages, then ask how many men share one avoided attack.
steps: About 42 men treated for five years per heart attack prevented
reference: Shepherd et al., Prevention of coronary heart disease with pravastatin in men with hypercholesterolemia, New England Journal of Medicine, 1995
